title: Built a cozy game to help me learn Japanese
author: thetinytrex
selftext:
I used to study Japanese in my free time for fun and would use WaniKani and Anki (both familiar names to anyone who has tried to self-study Japanese) and I wanted to make that experience more enjoyable for myself. So I built a cozy village game about restoring your family's shrine overridden by corrupted yokai. Inspired by the anime Natsume Yujincho, you help purify yokai, fulfill requests for them, have conversations with them, cook for them, fish, and restore your family's shrine to its rightful glory. Yokai move into the shrine and become friends, making the shrine feel lively. Your Japanese learning progress can be mirrored in the game as you befriend more yokai and repair more of the shrine.   
  
I built this for myself and have no plans to sell it. I just enjoyed the process and actually find the fishing and chanting very fun and therapeutic. Built entirely in Opus 5.5 except for Suno for the bgm. I'm still working on more mission features and cooking recipes, but most of the game is there, particularly the studying part. It also uses a spaced-repetition system like with Anki to help resurface words that you've gotten stuck on or need reviewing.

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body:
Wow thanks for the interest! I'll see what I can put together. I absolutely love Japan too. It's easily my favorite destination. I've been about 5 times in my life and would go every year if I could.  
  
The Japanese in the game is AI translated, but from my experience so far, it matches with what I used with Wanikani. Although, I'm sure your wife might spot mistakes. I also want to finish the yokai missions and flesh out the cooking a bit more before I publish it but I'll do a follow up when it's ready!

replies.author: Flope
replies.body:
~ While we are waiting for OP to release their game ~

I now live in Japan and speak fluently but when I was first starting I found resources like  [Tae Kim](https://guidetojapanese.org/learn/) and [Fuji Learning](https://fujilearning.com/) helpful. Japanese Ammo on YouTube is also good if you learn better with video. 

For your next trip you could start by just learning Katakana which is pretty quick to do and will let you understand a ton of vocab while traveling. Good ruck 👍

replies.author: darkoblivion000
replies.body:
Thanks that’s really helpful! I will look into these 

Living in Japan sounds like the dream but I hear once you are a resident they treat you differently and also working there can be difficult, is that true?

replies.author: Flope
replies.body:
No prob! Well Japan is an ethnically homogeneous country so in a sense yeah you will always be seen as not-Japanese, it will be obvious before you even begin speaking. But that doesn't mean people are mean or don't like you. Our neighbors are great and often invite us to local community events and stuff, in fact we just participated in a neighborhood sports meet yesterday and won some dish soap! lol 

Working conditions also vary a lot by company, it seems like each passing year the work culture is becoming a little more relaxed but yes there are still many workplaces (most?) that would be considered difficult by western standards.

comments.author: spfy
comments.body:
I've been struggling to successfully learn japanese for a long long time. I've learned thousands of cards with anki for kanji, vocab. Did grammar with bunpro. Tried other alternatives like jpdb, subtitle tutor method, etc. I always eventually trail off it and stall.  
This might be really nice for me. But I'm curious, did you hardcode in a certain kanji/vocab progression? Does it eventually run out? Does it have a sort of SRS mechanism underneath to track what you've learned? Is there any sort of AI integration to keep the learning going indefinitely with the conversations?

replies.author: thetinytrex
replies.body: Yes, it does have an SRS mechanism like Anki. But it doesn't have any AI integrations. Since I built this for me, I didn't go that crazy into the language development other than what I did with Wanikani. The vocabulary is hardcover as big json files split up by approximate N5 to N1 levels. I might consider AI integration as a future feature but what's there is more than enough for me to last a while studying the vocabulary. I was planning on custom vocabulary like what you can do with Anki but haven't gotten there. AI conversations would be really cool and I'll have to look into it. Maybe let the player input their own API key.
